The food is somewhat okay and acceptable, but unfortunately the service is extremely poor and the overall atmosphere is very unpleasant.
I understand that it’s an open space and that customers are allowed to smoke, but the café is clearly greedy. Tables are placed ridiculously close to each other, to the point where you feel like you’re sitting with the people next to you. As a result, if someone is smoking, you’re the one who suffers the most.
Honestly, it is not worth visiting at all...

title: Classic Rock Coffee Co
text_raw: روحنا الساعة ١م تقريبا و الوايتر خد وقت عشان يظهر و ياخد الاوردر. طلبنا فطار انا و صحابي ، هما طلبوا american breakfast beef bacon و انا طلبت smoked beef breakfast. الاكل اتأخر اوي و لما نزل طلع الاوردر مش مظبوط و بالاخص الطبق بتاعي. المفروض ان البطاطس تبقي hash brown و جتلي بطاطس محمرة عادية، البيف المشوي بقي شرايح سموكد بيف من اي سوبرماركت ، المفروض يبقي فيه خس كابوتشا iceberg و مجاش (و لما سألت الويتر فين الخس اللي المفروض ينزل مع الطبق، قالي شكل الطبق اللي نزل ده هو الصح ، و راح جابلي طبق صغير فيه شرايح خيار و طماطم و زيتون اسود)، محطوط ٣ مشرومات صغيرين جدا، و اخيرا ليس اخرا البيض انا طلباه بينيدكت benedict (هما كاتبين في المنيو اننا نختار اي نوع بيض عايزينه بدل الاومليت) و جالي شكله اومليت (مرفق صورة لوصف الطبق في المنيو و صورة للفطار اللي جالي علي الواقع). ف طبعا ناديت الوايتر و قولتلوا ان الطبق مش مظبوط خالص و ان البيض ده اكيد معمول غلط ف قالي انه حاضر هيدخل للشيف يظبطهولي. الاكل اتأخر اوي و صحابي كانوا قربوا يخلصوا اكل . جابلي الطبق اخيرا و طلع زي الطبق الاول بالظبط، مع اختلاف ان البيض بدل ما هو اومليت متطبق ٤ اربع بقي جايلي قطعة واحدة شبه البان كيك. قولتلوا يا عم ده مش بينيدكت خالص! .. قالي تحبي الغي الاوردر قولتله لا خلاص انا جعانة و صحابي بيخلصوا اكلهم. لما جينا نحاسب ظهر لنا المدير عشان ندفع بالفيزا ف اشتكيت و حكيتله اللي حصل, قالي معلش انا اسف بس المنيو اتعدلت و احنا لسه مغيرناش الqr code بتاع المنيو اللي علي الترابيزات ف حقك عليا. قولتله المفروض ان تقول للوايتر ان لما حد يطلب الطبق ده تنبهه ان الطبق اتغير خالص . و انتهي الكلام علي كده. المكان نفسه مش وحش لكن مش عارفة هاروحلهم تاني ولا لا بعد المقلب ده.

text_raw:
I came in with an old friend looking for a place to sit, catch up, and grab drinks. While browsing the menu, we were considering a few food options, but when we started by ordering just drinks, the manager immediately stopped us—refusing to serve us unless we ordered food. He claimed "they are a restaurant, not a cafe" and were afraid people would sit for hours with laptops.

Since we were busy catching up and didn't want the hassle of leaving to find another spot, we gave in and ordered dessert with our drinks just to stay. Sadly, both the drinks and desserts were mediocre at best.

The logic here is completely absurd. The place was almost empty when we arrived, and completely empty by the time we left. I even tried to give the manager polite, constructive feedback—warning him that enforcing rigid rules out of fear of hypothetical laptop campers was hurting his own business more than anything—but he just kept stubbornly insisting on his policy.

Great restaurants focus on welcoming guests and building goodwill, not treating paying customers with pre-baked mistrust. Unbelievably poor business logic. Save your time and go somewhere that actually understands hospitality.

If I could give less than one star, I absolutely would.

The quality was extremely disappointing. Don’t let anyone convince you to order from Al Raai. As shown in the video, the fava beans were more like bean soup, and the falafel was completely soaked in oil.

When I called to complain, all I received was an apology—just like many other restaurants I encountered during my vacation. Unfortunately, apologies are always available, but actual solutions are nowhere to be found.

The restaurant manager politely called me, apologized, and promised to send a replacement order of fava beans. I waited for an entire hour, but nothing arrived. When I called him again, I received yet another apology.

Honestly, I am extremely disappointed and deeply dissatisfied with both the food quality and the customer service. A truly “wonderful” restaurant—with “excellent” service and quality. Absolutely disgusting! 😡😡

title: The Kolbasti Lounge
text_raw:
I had to update my review after the amazing attitude from both the owner and the team at Kolbasti Kitchen.

My first experience honestly wasn’t great. I ordered the Kolbasti Chicken, Kolbasti Beef, and Lasagna. The chicken was okay, but it didn’t really live up to the expectations built from the branding and videos. I really didn’t enjoy the beef, and the lasagna also wasn’t for me.

What made me change my review was how the team handled everything. They actually reached out to me, listened to my feedback, and genuinely wanted a chance to make things right. They insisted I give them another try and even refused to let me pay for the replacement order.

I ended up trying the steak and pasta this time, and honestly, both were really, really good.

More than the food itself, I genuinely appreciated the way they dealt with me. You can tell they care about customer experience and take feedback seriously, and I really respect that.

Wishing them all the best and continued success inshaAllah.

title: Paul
text_raw:
We went there last night at around 10:30 PM.

When we entered, we looked at the food displayed in the glass display cases at the counter, then waited at the cashier to place our order(around 7 mins) . However, no one came to serve us, take our order, or even simply tell us, “Please have a seat, and we’ll come to serve you.”

Then, an employee came behind the cashier, shouting and throwing plates around!

So we decided to sit down, thinking that perhaps someone would come and take our order. However, we found the table dirty and covered with leftover croissant crumbs.

We waited for a while, but still no one came to take our order, so we eventually left because the atmosphere was unpleasant.

Why isn’t there a dedicated employee at the cashier to take customers’ orders? If there isn’t one, why didn’t anyone simply tell us to have a seat and that someone would come to serve us? And why was an employee shouting in a place that is supposed to be relaxing?

Overall, the atmosphere simply does not match the standard or character of the place.

title: Paul
text_raw:
The worst experience you could possibly have when you’re simply trying to go out, relax, and sit somewhere that is supposed to be upscale.

We walked in normally, like any other customers, and took some time looking at the pastries and displays to decide what we wanted.

We stood there. And stood there. And stood there. Completely ignored.

The staff were walking back and forth behind the counter, yet nobody even bothered to acknowledge us or look our way. After a while, one employee finally came over, threw a plate onto the counter, and said: “انا طالعة عين امي”.

Then he started banging on the counter aggressively. There was absolutely no respect or basic courtesy, as if we weren’t even there.

I told the person I was with, “Let’s just sit down since the situation is like this.” We went to a table, only to find it dirty and covered in croissant crumbs.

We sat there for a while, and once again, nobody came to take our order. The entire atmosphere felt tense, unwelcoming, and completely unpleasant. It was the kind of atmosphere that makes you want to get up and leave rather than sit there for even a minute.

After all of that, we simply walked out.

Honestly, I cannot imagine anyone in their right mind willingly coming back after being treated this way. One of the worst cafés I’ve ever experienced when it comes to cleanliness, hospitality, and basic respect. Definitely not the upscale experience you would expect from a place like this.

That’s not a problem in itself, but it should be clearly stated on the menu to avoid any unpleasant surprises.

The taste is still good, but the service is truly disappointing.

The staff spoke Arabic among themselves, assuming I didn’t understand, which is very inappropriate.

Despite high prices and tips that are supposed to go to the employees, the welcome and follow-up fall short: I asked for a different dish, was told “yes,” and then no one ever came back.

In summary: good food, poor service.

text_raw:
I ordered pizza from Daje recently. Overall, it was okay- not bad, but it could definitely be improved.

The Margherita pizza was a bit disappointing. The cheese didn’t have much flavour, and the dough felt more like bread dough than proper pizza dough- quite soft and not the typical pizza texture you’d expect. I wish they had used Gouda or high-quality mozzarella instead of what seems to be local Egyptian mozzarella.

On the other hand, the mushroom pizza was very good- great taste, nicely balanced, and I’d definitely order that one again.

The waiting time was also a bit long, but I can excuse that.

Recommendation: Try improving the cheese quality- Gouda or real mozzarella would make a big difference.

​A bit price-wise on the higher end, but completely worth it for unmatched quality.

title: Al Beiruti Garden 8
text_raw:
No matter how many Lebanese restaurants open in Cairo, Al Beiruti at Garden8  will always be one of my favorites. We went as a party of three and ordered a proper Lebanese spread, and honestly, most of it reminded me why I keep coming back.

I’ll start with the dishes that impressed me the least.

The warak enab was good, but it needed more of a kick. I wanted more lemon, acidity, or pomegranate molasses to give the filling that extra zing 6/10

The msakhan rolls were another miss for me. I liked the charred bread on the outside, but the filling lacked flavor, and the char itself added a slightly bitter taste that overpowered everything 5/10

Now onto the good stuff 😋

The mutabbal was smoky and silky smooth, with bursts of freshness from the pomegranate seeds and a lovely tang from the pomegranate molasses. The combination of smoky sweet eggplant, acidity and crunch was just beautiful 9/10

The hummus with minced meat and pine nuts was honestly perfect. The hummus was creamy and smooth, with just the right seasoning, while the meat and pine nuts added richness, flavor and texture. It didn’t need anything else 10/10

The fattoush was decent with the acidity I like, and I loved the crunchy za’atar crackers they added. They did feel a little stale, though, which took away from the experience 7/10

The batata harra came hot and crispy, with a lovely bite. good plate to share. 7/10.

But my personal favorite savory dish was the ras asfour with mustard sauce. The meat was incredibly flavorful, coated in that delicious mustard sauce, and we honestly licked the plate clean. It came with potato wedges, which I suspect were there to soak up all that sauce, but the potatoes themselves needed more seasoning. The meat was absolutely delicious 9/10

For dessert, we tried the halawet jibn, filled with what I believe was ashta and served with simple syrup on the side. It was good, but nothing particularly memorable for me 6/10

The real star was the مفروكة الفستقThat combination of crispy, crushed kunafa, fresh ashta and crunchy pistachios, finished with simple syrup, was everything. The textures were spot on, the sweetness was perfectly balanced, and every bite was just beautiful. Easily my favorite dessert of the meal10/10

The Arabic coffee was also really good and the perfect way to finish the meal.

Service was very good throughout. The manager came by to check on us, and the bread basket was replenished regularly, which I always appreciate.

Overall, a solid 9/10 experience, it’s on the expensive side, but for me, the food, atmosphere and service make it worth it. A couple of dishes could be better, but Al Beiruti remains a favorite and I’ll definitely keep coming back.

Ahmed Nada Restaurant (مطعم أحمد ندا) in the Fifth District is a good choice if you enjoy traditional Egyptian oriental food, especially grilled dishes and kebab. The food was good during my visit, and the restaurant is worth considering if you are looking for an oriental dining experience with family or friends.

One of the things I liked most was the outdoor seating area. In my opinion, the outdoor atmosphere is much nicer than the indoor seating on the first floor. Sitting outside gives you a more enjoyable dining experience and makes the place feel more comfortable and suitable for a relaxed meal, especially when the weather is pleasant.

The food itself was satisfying, particularly the oriental dishes and kebab. If you are a fan of Egyptian grilled food, this is one of the main reasons to give the restaurant a try.

However, I have one suggestion for improvement regarding the music. I think the choice of songs could be better suited to the restaurant's atmosphere. Changing the playlist to something more appropriate for an oriental restaurant would make the overall experience more enjoyable and create a better ambiance for customers.
Overall, Ahmed Nada is a good option in the Fifth District for oriental food and kebab. I would personally recommend choosing the outdoor seating rather than the indoor area on the first floor for a better atmosphere. With some improvement to the music selection, the dining experience could be even better.
